title: Hotfix: Privileged role escalation via SSO assertion in Private deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-severity bug reported by two enterprise Private customers: an improperly validated SAML/SSO assertion can lead to role elevation in Private control plane deployments. The assertion-processing path in the private auth proxy mistakenly trusts an attribute mapping when the Identity Provider drops the 'roles' claim, causing fallback to a default admin role mapping. This can be triggered during IdP migration or atypical SAML responses and has been reproduced in customer environments and our staging clusters.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure Private control plane with SAML SSO and custom attribute mapping for roles
2) Send a SAML response without the 'roles' attribute but with 'email' and 'name' attributes present
3) Observe that auth proxy fallback path performs a legacy mapping which assigns 'admin' instead of rejecting the assertion
4) Use the elevated session token to call /v1/admin/* endpoints and verify privileged actions succeed
root_cause_analysis: Edge case in the SSO assertion normalization: when the 'roles' attribute is missing, the mapper uses an undocumented legacy fallback (legacy_role_map) that contains a wildcard mapping to 'admin' for compatibility with old on-prem setups. There is no explicit allow-listing of accepted role values in the private control plane, and audit-log hooks are delayed until after session creation, so short-lived elevated sessions may occur before audit entries are written.
mitigation: 1) Immediate: deploy a gate that rejects SSO assertions which do not include an explicit 'roles' or 'groups' claim to all affected Private customers (hot patch)
2) Notify impacted customers and recommend manual revoke of tokens/rotating sessions until patch is applied
3) Increase audit log retention window and add real-time alert if admin role is granted to a new session for accounts with no prior admin activity
proposed_fix: Remove legacy_role_map fallback and enforce strict role validation: if the mapped role is not in the tenant's allowed role set, reject the assertion. Implement a schema validation step during assertion parsing and make role mapping deterministic. Also add a feature flag to allow gradual rollout for Private customers.
rollout_plan: A) Prepare hotfix branch that adds assertion gate and schema validation (runtime change only)
B) Stage deploy to internal staging and two non-production customer sandboxes: verify assertion rejection and no regression for normal SSO flows
C) Canary deploy to 10% of Private fleets with feature flag enabled and close monitoring (4h), then 50%, then 100%
D) After verification, merge into private-2026.03.1 release and schedule rolling update windows with customers
E) Run a backward-compat shim for customers on deprecated IdP setups for one release with warning logs and migration guidance
postmortem_notes: - Root cause: legacy compatibility code remained after refactor in 2024 and lacked unit tests for absent-roles case
- Action items: add assertion unit tests, add e2e SSO test matrix for missing-attribute scenarios, audit all legacy fallbacks in auth proxy
- Longer term: design an SSO compatibility guide and a migration utility for customers to verify IdP role mappings before switching
